title: Two brothers, two choices
hook: the giant tells his brother he's wrong, and goes to fight for him anyway
carry: dharma first, even before a brother

segments.voice: Yesterday: Kumbhakarna, the giant who sleeps for months, woken with drums and elephants because Ravana was losing. kumbhakarna is tamas: the sleep that misses what matters.

Kumbhakarna walks into Ravana's hall, still huge with sleep, and Ravana pours it all out. Rama has crossed the sea. Our best warriors are dead. I lost today. You're the only one left who can save us. The court waits for the giant's roar. And Kumbhakarna, the brother known for sleeping and eating, says what only Vibhishana has said to the king's face, and Vibhishana was driven out for it.
screen: `RAVANA POURS IT OUT.` → `YOU'RE THE ONLY ONE LEFT.` → `THE GIANT SPEAKS PLAINLY.`

segments.voice: We told you, he says. At your council, this is exactly what we said would happen. A king who acts first and thinks afterward, who ignores good advice, brings disaster on himself. You took another man's wife. This is the result. Ravana's face darkens. He wants a champion, not a lecture. And Kumbhakarna sees his brother hurting, and softens. Enough, he says. Whatever you did, I'm your brother. I'll go and kill your enemy. On the battlefield he's terrifying. The monkeys scatter, and Angada has to shame them into turning back. He seizes Sugriva and carries him off under his arm, until Sugriva tears at the giant's ears and nose and escapes. In the end Rama brings him down with his arrows. The Tamil poet Kamban adds a scene. Before the fight, Vibhishana comes to his brother on the field and begs him to join Rama. Kumbhakarna refuses gently: you did right, you stay with Rama; my place is with our brother. So the Ramayana sets two brothers side by side, and both told Ravana the truth to his face. One left to stand with dharma, what is right, and Rama welcomed him. The other let love for his brother carry him into a wrong war, and fell. Many readers admire Kumbhakarna's honesty and his loyalty. But the epic honors Vibhishana's choice. Telling the truth isn't enough if you then march with the wrong. Dharma first, even before a brother.
screen: `WE TOLD YOU THIS WOULD HAPPEN.` · `STILL, I'M YOUR BROTHER.` · `KAMBAN: YOU STAY WITH RAMA.` · `TWO BROTHERS, TWO CHOICES.` · then, large: `DHARMA FIRST, EVEN BEFORE A BROTHER.`

segments.voice: Think of someone you love who is doing something you know isn't right. If you pray, hold them before God by name, and ask for what Vibhishana had: the courage to be honest and kind at once. If you don't, breathe in their name, and breathe out the true thing you'd say to them, gently.
Kumbhakarna. The giant who tells Ravana plainly he's wrong, and then dies fighting for him out of a brother's loyalty, beside Vibhishana, who chose dharma.
Your line: dharma first, even before a brother. Lakshmana's best day, and his worst, is next. See you then.

screen: `DAY 646 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: RAMA, WHO KEEPS THE BOUNDS.`

howItsDone: Kumbhakarna's rebuke of Ravana and his loyalty are much discussed in Ramayana storytelling, and Kamban's Tamil scene of the two brothers, Vibhishana and Kumbhakarna, meeting on the battlefield is often recited.

fork.setup: your best friend is about to do something you know is wrong, and asks for your help. by the Ramayana's two brothers, what's dharma?
options: tell them the truth kindly, and don't join in.
say nothing and stay out of it.
fork.reveal: Kumbhakarna told the truth, then marched with the wrong anyway. Vibhishana told it and stood with dharma. the epic honors the second.

original.note: Sanskrit bhrātā: brother; the word at the heart of Kumbhakarna's answer to Ravana.

what a scholar hears: Kamban gives him a farewell scene with Vibhishana on the battlefield, which Valmiki does not have.

chat.meaning: Kumbhakarna told Ravana he was wrong, then fought for him anyway; the Ramayana honors Vibhishana's choice: dharma first, even before a brother.

tie.story: Kumbhakarna told Ravana that taking Sita was wrong, then marched out and died fighting for him because he was his brother.

Kumbhakarna.meaning: Ravana's giant brother, who warns him and fights for him

Kamban.meaning: a Tamil poet who retold the Ramayana

Sugriva.meaning: king of the monkeys, Rama's ally

Vibhishana.meaning: Ravana's younger brother, now on Rama's side

dharma.meaning: what is right; duty, the order that holds life together

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 62–63 (Kumbhakarna's rebuke and his promise)
Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 17–18 (Vibhishana comes to Rama and is welcomed)
Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 66–67 (Kumbhakarna in battle; Sugriva's escape; Kumbhakarna's death)
Kamba Ramayanam, Yuddha Kandam (Vibhishana meets Kumbhakarna on the battlefield)

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.

The head falling on Lanka (some versions add the body falling into the sea): confirm.

Original game: bhrātā and English 'brother' share a Proto-Indo-European root; a standard etymology, but confirm.
